messages.author: e1b65c2d8ed36d3a
messages.subject: Multiple subsets
parts:
Hi,

I have used Cardinal for a while and it's great to use!

I have just come across a small issue I have not yet been able to work around. I am wanting to take multiple subsets from the same MSImaging experiment with the following code:

# Creating subsets
daph35um_eggROI <- daphProc[, daph35um_eggROImask] 
daph35um_eggROI

daph35um_midgutROI <- daphProc[, daph35um_midgutROImask]
daph35um_midgutROI

However when I try to do this I get the following error:

Error in if (xrange[1L] == xrange[2L]) return(1) : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Do you have a work around for it? Or am I missing something?

Best wishes,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: Multiple subsets
parts:
Hey Matt,

To subset the dataset, I have been using the subsetPixels function. You can see some examples here: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/Cardinal/inst/doc/Cardinal-2-guide.html#summarization-e.g.-mean-spectra

messages.subject: Re: Multiple subsets
parts:
Thanks for your reply - I have now started using this approach as I find storing all the ROIs in the MSImaging object a lot neater!

For anyone coming to this topic later though the cause was that I had created my mask from a previous sample (due to a mistake in naming) and so the mask logical vector was longer than the number of pixels in the MSImaging object I wanted to subset.
